A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EnIGMA study, with inspectable main text, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H. The code omissions in v3 are visible document differences, rather than unresolved extraction gaps, and do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original EnIGMA evaluations across four CTF benchmarks, component ablations, leakage analyses, and challenge trajectories, including quantitative results in Table 2 and Appendices E–F.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark evaluations, ablations, leakage experiments, and qualitative case studies, with aggregate results in Table 1 and detailed results in the appendices.

M1.justification: The interactive tools, summarizers, demonstrations, and agent procedure are retained. Section 2.2 rephrases the LM summarizer as another LM agent, consistent with the separate summarizer prompts already documented in v2 Appendix G.2; this does not establish a procedural or backbone change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four benchmarks totaling 390 challenges, the same development set, and the same 21 CSAW 2024 challenges. v3 identifies the latter as qualifying-round challenges and gives their category counts; it does not introduce additional coverage.

E2.justification: The NYU, CyBench, InterCode-CTF, and Google DeepMind baseline systems are retained. v3 Table 2 supplies additional backbone-specific comparisons for existing baseline systems, without introducing a new comparison method.

E3.justification: New Table 2 extends the reported model-matched comparisons to CyBench-agent configurations using LLaMA 3.1 405B and GPT-4o. The retained EnIGMA model versions, pass@1 metric, $3 budget, temperature, sampling settings, and experiment samples remain unchanged; no reruns are established.

E4.justification: The component ablations, action-use analyses, temperature sensitivity experiment, soliloquy-suppression experiment, unseen-challenge evaluation, and Appendix H case studies retain their experimental questions and findings. The added significance reporting concerns an existing turn-count comparison.

E5.justification: Section 4.1 adds p = 0.019 to the existing comparison of 11.5 versus 14.9 turns with and without interactive tools. v2 reports those means without a p-value. v3 does not identify the statistical test or establish additional runs.

E6.justification: v3 Table 2 newly reports CyBench-agent scores of 7.5% with LLaMA 3.1 405B and 12.5% with GPT-4o. The existing EnIGMA benchmark scores, ablation results, leakage statistics, and unseen-challenge outcomes are retained; these additions do not demonstrate performance changes between versions.

T1.justification: The soliloquy and solution-leakage classification criteria in Appendix F are unchanged. Neither version adds formal theoretical results or proofs, and v3 introduces no substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: interactive tools and summarization for CTF agents, a development set, benchmark improvements, and analysis of soliloquizing and leakage. The extrapolation claim was already present in v2.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 adds an explicit explanatory link between fewer turns with interactive tools and the tendency to succeed quickly but fail slowly, attributing performance gains to the IAT framework. The existing leakage interpretations, failure analyses, and applicability caveats remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds API-pricing sources and an access link, qualifying-round identification, and category breakdown for the existing CSAW 2024 evaluation. Conversely, Appendix H loses technical content after percent signs, including debugger registers and decryption expressions visible in v2 on pages 39 and 42, reducing reproducibility of those records.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to OpenAI, Anthropic, and Together AI pricing documentation. The substantive related-work discussion and positioning relative to earlier cybersecurity agents remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds EnIGMA to the title and headers, updates affiliations and publication information, expands acknowledgments, and moves them before the impact statement. Local revisions clarify tool selection, summarization, and the unseen-challenge evaluation; the overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 2, relocates the ablation table and several figures, and expands Figure 2's annotation and caption. The visual design is largely retained, but Appendix H code listings visibly truncate text after percent signs, damaging otherwise retained trajectory displays.

improvement.justification: v3 improves comparison transparency through Table 2 and adds useful dataset, pricing, and significance information, although the new p-value lacks a specified test. These limited gains coexist with confirmed loss of technical code content in Appendix H, making supporting trajectories less verifiable and reusable. With the central experiments and conclusions unchanged, the net quality direction is uncertain.
